:::{#def-prediction}
#### Prediction

A **prediction** of a random variable $Y$ is a constant $\hy$,
or a function $\hat{Y} \eqdef g(X)$ of another observable random variable $X$,
used as a guess for the value $Y$ takes:

$$\hy \quad \text{or} \quad \hat{Y} \eqdef g(X)$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-prediction}
#### Predictions of a die roll

Let $Y$ be the number shown by a fair six-sided die.
The constant $\hy = 3$ is a [prediction](#def-prediction) of $Y$.

Let $X$ be the indicator that $Y$ is even.
The function $g(X) = 2 + 2X$ is also a prediction of $Y$:
it guesses $2$ when $Y$ is odd and $4$ when $Y$ is even.

:::

::: {#rem-prediction-random}
#### A prediction from a random input is random

When no covariate or feature is available,
a prediction is a single number $\hy$ (such as a constant $c$).
When an informative random variable $X$ is observed,
a prediction is a function $g(X)$,
which is itself a random variable because $X$ is random.

:::
